Command: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land
Summary: Exodus 34:12 warns Israel, at the renewal of the covenant after the golden calf, to make no covenant with the inhabitants of the land, 'lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee.' Treaties would have bound Israel to peoples whose altars and worship it was commanded to destroy.
Commandment: Make no covenant with the inhabitants of the land.
Application: The command belonged to the conquest generation; its principle endures wherever an alliance would bind God's people to idolatry. Agreements are weighed by whether they protect or endanger faithfulness.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee (Exodus 34:12).
Function: A duty of character, given in Israel's form: the Law here shapes how people live. Exodus 34:12 warns Israel, at the renewal of the covenant after the golden calf. Scripture gives the reason: lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee. The fence was practical.
